title: Aggregates of ±inf and NaN: IEEE results, no raise
description: `sum` and `avg` of inf and -inf are NaN; `variance` and `stddev` of a set with an infinity are NaN; `sum(1e308, 1e308)` and `avg` are +inf, while `variance(1e308, 1e308)` is 0.0. A NaN input makes `sum`, `avg`, `variance` NaN; `min` skips it (it sorts last) and `max` returns it. None of this raises under ANSI.
`COVAR_*` and `CORR` follow `variance`: a NaN or ±inf input makes them NaN, under ANSI too.
reference: `nan_creation`: raise (#257); a statistical aggregate of ±inf raises (`stat_degenerate`); a sum past the largest double raises (#575). ST-3 and ST-5 record that Substrait leaves both open. Spark needs guards.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `sum` of NaN is NaN, no error under ANSI

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.

evidence.sql: SELECT var_samp(x) AS var_samp, var_pop(x) AS var_pop, stddev_samp(x) AS stddev_samp, stddev_pop(x) AS stddev_pop, covar_samp(x, y) AS covar_samp, covar_pop(x, y) AS covar_pop, corr(x, y) AS corr FROM (VALUES (CAST(1.0 AS DOUBLE), CAST(1.0 AS DOUBLE)), (CAST('NaN' AS DOUBLE), CAST(2.0 AS DOUBLE)), (CAST(2.0 AS DOUBLE), CAST(3.0 AS DOUBLE))) AS t(x, y)
